title: Principles Of Toxicology
mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a variant of immunoaffinity purification and is a means to remove a protein from a complex mixture in a highly specific manner."
Immunoprecipitation is a variant of immunoaffinity purification and is a means to remove a protein from a complex mixture in a highly specific manner.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the critical factor in determining how deeply a given gas penetrates into the lung."
Water solubility is the critical factor in determining how deeply a given gas penetrates into the lung.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is known to occur in many groups of animals, the primary interest and the focus of most research is in human cancer."
Human Cancer Although cancer is known to occur in many groups of animals, the primary interest and the focus of most research is in human cancer.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is used to determine whether or not a gene of interest is present as well as its copy number."
Southern analysis is used to determine whether or not a gene of interest is present as well as its copy number.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a syndrome in which the decrease in marrow production is limited to the erythroid lineage."
Pure red cell aplasia is a syndrome in which the decrease in marrow production is limited to the erythroid lineage.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a biocide that has antibacterial and antifungal properties."
ZPT is a biocide that has antibacterial and antifungal properties.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is any morphological or functional alteration caused by chemical or physical insult that interferes with normal growth, homeostasis, development, differentiation, and/or behavior."

Developmental toxicity is any morphological or functional alteration caused by chemical or physical insult that interferes with normal growth, homeostasis, development, differentiation, and/or behavior.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are the main effectors of fibrosis, although myofibroblasts play a substantial supporting role, especially in the deposition of collagen fibres throughout the canalicular tracts of the liver lobule."

Activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) are the main effectors of fibrosis, although myofibroblasts play a substantial supporting role, especially in the deposition of collagen fibres throughout the canalicular tracts of the liver lobule.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an endogenous compound released from skeletal muscle at a constant rate under most circumstances."
Creatinine is an endogenous compound released from skeletal muscle at a constant rate under most circumstances.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a very sensitive method used to measure minute quantities of an antigen."
Radioimmunoassay (RIA) is a very sensitive method used to measure minute quantities of an antigen.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the process through which cancer develops."
Carcinogenesis is the process through which cancer develops.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the fact that these alterations often occur in the absence of any clinical signs of toxicity."
Even more relevant is the fact that these alterations often occur in the absence of any clinical signs of toxicity.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the extent to which neurologic disability may be related to chronic low-level exposures, nor do we understand the overall impact of environmental contaminants on brain function."
Unknown is the extent to which neurologic disability may be related to chronic low-level exposures, nor do we understand the overall impact of environmental contaminants on brain function.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a biconvex transparent body, encased in an elastic capsule, and located between the pupil and the vitreous humor."
The lens is a biconvex transparent body, encased in an elastic capsule, and located between the pupil and the vitreous humor.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to inflammation of the portion of the optic nerve posterior to the globe."
Retrobulbar optic neuritis refers to inflammation of the portion of the optic nerve posterior to the globe.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an alteration that produces a stop codon and results in a truncated protein."
A nonsense mutation is an alteration that produces a stop codon and results in a truncated protein.
fib: ______ is the formation of chemical bonds between foreign chemicals and hydrophilic substances already present in the liver, thereby forming a diverse class of metabolites known as conjugates.
defining characteristic

A defining characteristic is the formation of chemical bonds between foreign chemicals and hydrophilic substances already present in the liver, thereby forming a diverse class of metabolites known as conjugates.
______ is the 50% size as the mean bisects the curve.
geometric mean
The geometric mean is the 50% size as the mean bisects the curve.
______ is an alkaloid pharmaceutical used in the treatment of gout, familial Mediterranean fever, and other disorders.
Colchicine
Colchicine is an alkaloid pharmaceutical used in the treatment of gout, familial Mediterranean fever, and other disorders.
______ is the proper measurement for particles that are deposited by impaction and sedimentation.
Aerodynamic diameter
Aerodynamic diameter is the proper measurement for particles that are deposited by impaction and sedimentation.
______ are defined by the characteristics of their cytoplasmic granules as they appear on a blood smear stained with a polychromatic (Romanovsky) stain.
Granulocytes
Granulocytes are defined by the characteristics of their cytoplasmic granules as they appear on a blood smear stained with a polychromatic (Romanovsky) stain.
______ are a set of proteins particular to the lens that, through their close intermolecular structure, give the lens both transparency and the proper refractive index.
water- soluble crystallins
The water- soluble crystallins are a set of proteins particular to the lens that, through their close intermolecular structure, give the lens both transparency and the proper refractive index.
______ is a poisonous substance produced within living cells or organisms; synthetic toxicants created by artificial processes are thus excluded.
toxin
A toxin is a poisonous substance produced within living cells or organisms; synthetic toxicants created by artificial processes are thus excluded.
______ is a permanent alteration in the genetic information (DNA) of the cell.
mutation
A mutation is a permanent alteration in the genetic information (DNA) of the cell.
______ are known to accumulate Ca2+ in lethally injured cells through a low-affinity, high-capacity Ca2+ transport system.
Mitochondria
Mitochondria are known to accumulate Ca2+ in lethally injured cells through a low-affinity, high-capacity Ca2+ transport system.
______ is an autonomously replicating DNA molecule and the inserted DNA segment may be as large as a gene or a small as a few nucleotides.
vector
The vector is an autonomously replicating DNA molecule and the inserted DNA segment may be as large as a gene or a small as a few nucleotides.
______ is the demonstration that some developmental immunotoxicants seem capable of inducing targeted immune suppression while at the same time elevating the risk of allergy and/or autoimmunity.
Adding to the complexity

Adding to the complexity is the demonstration that some developmental immunotoxicants seem capable of inducing targeted immune suppression while at the same time elevating the risk of allergy and/or autoimmunity.
______ is regarded as among the more common serious effects of xenobiotics, particularly drugs (Vandendries and Drews, 2006).
Primary toxicity
Primary toxicity is regarded as among the more common serious effects of xenobiotics, particularly drugs (Vandendries and Drews, 2006).
______ is the study of adverse effects of drugs, nontherapeutic chemicals and other agents in our environment on blood and blood- forming tissues (Bloom, 1997).
Hematotoxicology
Hematotoxicology is the study of adverse effects of drugs, nontherapeutic chemicals and other agents in our environment on blood and blood- forming tissues (Bloom, 1997).
______ is an important factor in the deposition of submicrometer particles.
Diffusion
Diffusion is an important factor in the deposition of submicrometer particles.
______ is a specialized area of embryology.
Teratology
Teratology is a specialized area of embryology.
